summary: Backend-only testing for NEW Max Energy Muay Thai Academy features. Created /app/backend/tests/test_new_features.py with 25 tests covering: admin login + is_admin flag, /api/auth/me admin check, classes category filter (Kids/Adults/all), 4 membership plans, announcements sorted pinned-first, /api/gym/info payload, membership apply (full nested details incl. medical + waiver + media consent) creating application + notification + listed in /me, admin-guards on 5 endpoints for anonymous (401) and member (403) callers (10 parametrized cases), admin overview counts, admin classes CRUD (create + list + update + delete + 404 after delete), admin announcement create + public visibility + delete, admin list applications + approve status + member notification, and Stripe booking/checkout regression. All 25 new tests PASS. Also updated legacy test_backend.py to align stale seed-count assertions with seed v3 (classes >=40 instead of >=70, events >=3 instead of >=4) and made payments test resilient under pytest-xdist parallelization. Full suite: 41/41 pass.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~910 lines (single file). Approaching the 700-line split threshold; consider splitting into routers (auth, classes, bookings, payments, membership, admin, events, announcements) for future maintainability.
seed_data() reseeds catalog collections whenever SEED_VERSION changes, but membership_applications and users are preserved correctly — safe.
Admin guard is Bearer-only for the JWT path; if an admin uses Emergent Google session_token (session cookie flow), the is_admin flag is honored from DB — verified via require_admin path.

membership/apply awaits send_email twice sequentially (gym + applicant). Best-effort try/except inside send_email handles email service failures, so /apply does not fail on email errors (matches spec).
Admin overview does not currently distinguish between members and admins in 'members' count — includes admin user. Minor; documented for main agent.
All Mongo queries correctly project out _id. No ObjectID leakage detected in responses.
